resources.string: ReelsBlock uses accessibility access for Instagram only to cover blocked Home posts and move away from Reels browsing, and hide the Explore grid while keeping Search usable. It never saves Instagram text and has no internet access. Disable it at any time in Accessibility settings.
On Android 13+, if access is restricted, open Settings → Apps → ReelsBlock → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings, then enable ReelsGuard in Accessibility.

ReelsGuard covers ads, suggested posts, and inline reels on Instagram Home, and moves away from Reels browsing. Reels shared in DMs stay viewable with a single-reel lock. Block Explore hides the discovery grid while keeping Search and profiles usable.

ReelsBlock needs accessibility access to recognize Instagram screens, cover ads, suggested posts and inline reels on Home, and move away from Reels browsing. Android grants access to on-screen content; this service is restricted to Instagram. Reels shared in DMs stay viewable with a single-reel lock.

Text and description matching happens in memory against fixed labels only. Instagram text will never be logged, saved, or transmitted. The app has no internet access and never likes, follows, comments, messages, or posts.

Consent, toast, diagnostics, auto-skip, Explore, and end-of-followed-content settings are saved locally. Show toast is off by default and gives brief fixed blocking feedback when enabled. Block Explore is on by default; it covers the discovery grid and backs out of discovery viewers while keeping Search and profiles usable. The end wall is on by default and also stops after three consecutive blocked groups; you can change this count. It covers Older posts and keeps stories usable. Auto-skip is off by default; when enabled, it scrolls Home forward once per blocked group. Debug mode is off by default. When enabled, it sends structural signals and action outcomes to Logcat only; the app never creates log files. Debug builds also permit on-demand node structure dumps containing fixed-label booleans and no raw text or descriptions.

Tap Agree to continue, then select ReelsGuard in Android Accessibility settings and turn it on. You can turn it off there at any time.
Log structural signals and action outcomes to Logcat only. Off by default. Debug builds also allow on-demand redacted tree dumps.
